reconciliation: These look contradictory and are not. Littler surveys EMPLOYERS on whether a formal AI policy exists anywhere in the organization. SHRM surveys HR PROFESSIONALS on whether a formal AI USE policy governs workforce use. Different populations, different question. Both may be cited; neither may be paraphrased as 'the share of organizations with an AI policy' without saying which instrument.

claims.claim: 68% of employers have a formal AI policy, roughly double the 38% a year earlier
51% of organizations have no formal AI use policy at all
claims.source: SHRM, State of AI in HR 2026

claims.claim: Of organizations that have a policy, about a quarter believe it is clear and future-proof; 54% say theirs is too restrictive and tied to specific current tools; a further 23% say theirs is too broad to guide behaviour
44% of US workers say their employer has no clear AI policy, or they do not know whether one exists

cautions: The failed figure: '~1% of organizations have a written AI policy' does NOT hold and must never be used. It appears in no shipped module; it survived only in a comp outline bullet until C-06.
